div.l: To riden bi þe weye domb as a stoon
And þ̉erfore wil I maken yow disport
As I . seyd arst and don yow som comfort
And yf yow lyketh alle bi oon assent
Forto stonden at my Iugement
And for to werken as I schal yow seie
To morwen whan we riden bi þe weie
Now by my fadir soule þat is ded
But ye be merye I wil yeue yow my hed
Hold vp your hondes wit oute more speche
Our conseill was not longe to seche
Vs þought it was noght worth to make it wys
And gᵃrauntede him wit oute more auys
And bad him seie his veordyt as him leste
Lordinges qdquod he now herkeneþ for þe beste
But take it nought I pᵃray yow in disdeigne
This is þe poynt to speke short ⁊and pleigne
That ech of yow to shorte wiþ our weye
In þis viage schal telle tales tweye
To Canturbery ward I mene it so
And homwardes he schal tellen oþ̉ere two
Of auentures þat whilom haue by falle
And which of yow þat bereþ hym best of alle
Þat is to seyn þat telleþ in this caas
Tales of beste sentence ⁊and most solaas
Shal haue a soꝑper at our aldercost
Here in þis place sitting by this post
Whan þat we comyn agayn fro Canturbury
And for to make yow þe more mery
I wil my selfen goodli wit ȝow ryde
Ryght at myn oune coste ⁊and be youre gyde
And who so wil myn Iuggement withsey
Shal pay all þat we spende bi þe weye
And yf ye vouchesaf þat it be soo
Tel me a noon with owten worde moo
And I . wil erly shape me þ̉er fore
This thing was gᵃraunted and our othes swore
Wit ful glad herte ⁊and pyȝen him also
That he wolde vouchesaf for to do soo
And þat he wolde be oure goủernoure
And of oure tales Iugge and reportour
